surprises.head: Florida shortened their bench
surprises.body: Florida’s bottom-six forwards played 34% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: The Panthers beat the Blackhawks
paras: Ryan Greene opened the scoring for the Blackhawks early in the first, but Sandis Vilmanis made it 1-1 for Florida a little over four minutes later. Matthew Tkachuk put the Panthers ahead 2-1 on the power play midway through the period. Roman Kantserov tied it up for Chicago midway through the second, but that was the last goal the Blackhawks would get. Lars Eller scored his first goal for Florida with less than three minutes left to put the Panthers ahead for good.

The Panthers outshot the Blackhawks 33-21, but the Blackhawks’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Akira Schmid made 19 saves for the Panthers, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 33 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Seth Jones, by our Swing measure.
The Panthers killed all seven Blackhawks power plays. The Cats moved to 6-4-2, sixth in the Atlantic, while the Blackhawks fell to 3-8-0, still last in the Central.

items.text: Sam Reinhart tied Stephen Weiss for fifth on the Panthers’ all-time scoring list, with 394 points.
The Blackhawks are on a three-game losing streak.
The Panthers’ Carter Verhaeghe played his 500th NHL game and had an assist.
The Panthers have beaten the Blackhawks four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
